summary: Request: Per-event Ed25519 signatures + resume tokens for ordered audit export (legal hold)
description:
Issue summary:
Aurora Bank (enterprise) requests a legally defensible audit export that preserves strict ordering, provides a per-event cryptographic signature (Ed25519), and includes resume tokens so exports can be resumed or replayed deterministically for legal-hold and eDiscovery. They require a sample delivery bundle and verification instructions for their internal auditors.

Background:
Customer ingests high volume of events (auth, prompt/response metadata, admin actions) and must produce an ordered archive for legal requests and SOC2 evidence. They want per-event signatures to prove non-repudiation and a small resume token that allows incremental replays without duplicating events. Customer also insists that user identifiers be pseudonymized with a deterministic HMAC using a rotating KEK, and that the export manifest includes checksums and attestation metadata (signer key id, timestamp, canonicalization method).

Request details / Acceptance criteria:
1) Export format: newline-delimited JSON (JSONL) gzip archive + manifest.json.
2) Each event object must include a top-level "sig" field containing an Ed25519 signature over the canonicalized event payload and headers. Signature format: base64url. Include "sig_kid" (key identifier) and "sig_ts" (UTC ISO8601).
3) Resume token: short opaque token (base64url) with a cryptographic anchor so that replay from token produces exact event sequence without overlap or gaps. Token TTL = 24h; tokens must be monotonic per-partition.
4) Pseudonymization: a deterministic HMAC-SHA256 of the subject identifier using customer-scoped KEK; provide sample mapping tool and rotation guidance. KEK rotation must allow backfill verification for previous KEKs via manifest.
5) Manifest must include: archive checksum (sha256), signer public key fingerprint, key attestation reference (HSM certificate chain link), canonicalization method (sorted keys, utf8 normalizing), and a per-archive signature (Ed25519) over the manifest.
6) Delivery options: S3 presigned (customer bucket) or SFTP with signed receipt. Provide both samples.
7) Verification guide: steps for auditors to verify per-event signatures and resume-token replays, including a small reference script and expected verification output.

Security & compliance constraints:
- Customer requires attested HSM signing (option A: Redwood HSM-signed keys with attestation; option B: customer-supplied public key and Redwood signs archives only).
- No cleartext PII may be exported; per-event payloads must contain pseudonymized identifiers only.
- All artifacts must be retained according to customer's legal-hold retention window (90 days initial request) and include a tamper-evident manifest.

Deadline:
Customer asks for an initial sample bundle and verification steps by 2026-03-18 to feed into their audit window.

Notes:
This request overlaps with prior audit export work but is distinct in asking for per-event Ed25519 signatures + resume tokens and a deterministic pseudonymization scheme that supports KEK rotation and verification.
steps_to_validate: 1) Receive sample gzip JSONL bundle and manifest.json. 2) Run provided verification script against manifest to verify archive checksum and manifest signature. 3) For each event, verify the 'sig' field using the signer public key and confirm 'sig_ts' within expected window. 4) Use resume token with replay endpoint to request events after token; confirm sequence matches archive and tokens do not cause duplication. 5) Confirm no raw PII fields are present and that pseudonymization mapping verifies deterministically with provided HMAC parameters.

investigation_notes: Checked existing audit-export pipeline: supports JSONL gzip bundles, manifest signing at archive level (currently RSA-2048). No existing per-event signature path.

Evaluated signing approaches: (A) Sign inline at ingestion (higher CPU, deterministic), (B) Sign during export worker (less impact on ingestion, still per-event cost). Export-worker approach preferred to avoid affecting real-time SLOs.

HSM attestation: Redwood HSM supports Ed25519 signing via PKCS#11 shim; need to confirm certificate chain export format for attestation reference. Latency tests show ~3-6ms per sign when batched; for 100k events/hour export-worker signing is acceptable with worker autoscaling.

Resume token design sketch: token = base64url( HMAC-SHA256( partition_id || seq_no || epoch ) || truncation ) with server-side monotonic seq mapping. Will wrap token in MAC to prevent exposure of internal ids.
Pseudonymization: use HMAC-SHA256 with customer KEK; deterministic output hex/base64. Provide sample rotation table in manifest mapping previous KEK IDs with start/end times.

Dependencies: platform PR to add per-event signing (https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6734). Need KMS/HSM team for attestation artifact and support for Ed25519 key material export (public key fingerprint only).
resolution: Triage complete. Engineering published initial design and opened PR. Awaiting engineering prototype of signed JSONL bundle and verifier script. Next steps: platform eng to deliver sample bundle by 2026-03-17; Support to coordinate secure delivery and auditor walkthrough. Follow-up item: confirm KEK rotation cadence with customer and produce runbook for verification steps.
